example_prompt: Update my orders when Gozem notifies me that a delivery was assigned, completed, canceled or expired.

input_schema.description: Envelope Gozem POSTs to your webhook URL when a subscribed event occurs.

account_guid.description: The account the event belongs to

event_type.description: The type of event that occurred. Courier events: courier.trip.created, courier.trip.assigned, courier.trip.at_pickup, courier.trip.started, courier.trip.completed, courier.trip.canceled, courier.trip.expired, courier.trip.stop.started, courier.trip.stop.completed, courier.trip.chat.message, courier.trip.payment.completed, courier.trip.payment.refunded

data.description: Event-specific payload; its contents depend on event_type

environment.description: sandbox or production, the environment the event came from

response_schema.description: Return a 2xx as soon as the event is accepted; the response body is not documented.

gotchas: Set a secret on the webhook in the Partner Portal: it is optional, and without it payloads aren't signed. With a secret, X-Webhook-Signature carries the hex HMAC SHA-256 of the raw request body — verify it on the raw bytes (not a re-serialized object) with a constant-time comparison, and reject a mismatch.

Return a 2xx as soon as the event is accepted and do the work in the background. Failed deliveries are retried up to three times, then marked failed; repeated failures can disable the webhook. Return 5xx only when your own storage is down — that is the one case where you want the retry.
The same event can arrive more than once: deduplicate on the envelope guid (EVT_…).

event_type is one of the courier.trip.* events (created, assigned, at_pickup, started, completed, canceled, expired, stop.started, stop.completed, chat.message, payment.completed, payment.refunded). New types get added: ignore types you don't know instead of failing. stop.started / stop.completed fire once per dropoff, even on a single-dropoff trip, per the lifecycle page — Getting Started mentions them only for trips with more than one dropoff.

data's content isn't documented beyond 'the resource the event is about' (stop events carry which dropoff was served and its delivery confirmation): this spec leaves it untyped. Read the trip with get_trip when you need its full state.
The envelope carries no timestamp and the signature covers only the body: no replay protection is documented. The retry delay is only 'a short delay'. Validate the payload shape before acting on it.
Treat courier.trip.canceled (by you, the driver or the system) and courier.trip.expired (no driver within the acceptance window, whose length isn't documented) as normal endings, not errors.

Events are delivered only to active webhooks of the API client's account subscribed to that event type; environment says whether the event comes from sandbox or production. The portal's Format option isn't documented: this example expects JSON. In sandbox, trip events fire only when you drive the trip with simulate_trip_state.

spans: The signature is an HMAC SHA-256 of the raw request body using your webhook secret.
Always verify against the raw body, not a re-serialized version, and use a constant-time comparison
the platform retries delivery up to three times with a short delay between attempts before marking the delivery failed
Repeated failures can cause a webhook to be disabled automatically
Handle events idempotently by tracking the event guid and ignoring ones you have already processed.
Event-specific payload; its contents depend on event_type
with a short delay between attempts
Validate the payload shape before acting on it.
Events are delivered only to webhooks that belong to the same account as the API client, are active, and are subscribed to that event type.
